- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If true outcome shows downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overfits to recent highs; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
